angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 560,108 km at 5.01 pc = 1.49 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 199.6080 +/- 0.1208 mas (same row, RUWE 1.94): 5.01 pc, no zero-point correction; the RUWE is high, so the astrometry fits a single star poorly, and the parallax is used as published
radiusSource: Radius 0.8051 +/- 0.0035 solar radii from Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 757, 112, Table 6, GJ 166A: radius in solar radii, 0.8051 +/- 0.0035, from the weighted mean of the interferometric measurements the table lists (https://doi.org/10.1088/0004-637X/757/2/112): 560,108 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.816 solar masses from Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 757, 112, Table 6, GJ 166A: mass 0.816 solar masses from the K-band mass-luminosity relation of Henry & McCarthy (1993), not a dynamical mass (https://doi.org/10.1088/0004-637X/757/2/112); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5147 +/- 14 K from Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 757, 112, Table 6, GJ 166A: effective temperature in K, 5147 +/- 14, from the weighted mean of the interferometric measurements the table lists (https://doi.org/10.1088/0004-637X/757/2/112). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 757, 112, Table 6, GJ 166A: effective temperature in K, 5147 +/- 14, from the weighted mean of the interferometric measurements the table lists (https://doi.org/10.1088/0004-637X/757/2/112)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/keid.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.538, rounded to two decimals
spectralTypeSource: SIMBAD, * omi02 Eri: spectral type K0V (1989ApJS...71..245K)
projectedRotationSpeedSource: SIMBAD, * omi02 Eri: projected rotation speed 9.21 km/s, the measurement SIMBAD prefers (2025A&A...704A..49B)

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
